title: Identification of extracellular matrix-associated signatures to establish a risk model in rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis through transcriptomic analysis.
authors: Huang, Biaojie; Huang, Yuhan; Lv, Ru; Wang, Weikai; Hu, Zhihao; Li, Guibo; Wei, Chen; Chen, Xi; Li, Zhengdong; Zhang, Xue
journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组和机器学习构建类风湿关节炎与骨关节炎的ECM相关风险模型，虽涉及转录因子调控网络预测，但核心是疾病诊断分型，缺乏蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA) frequently coexist, complicating diagnosis and treatment. The extracellular matrix (ECM) serves as a critical modulator of disease progression, coordinating multilayered matrix degradation and inflammatory cascades in both conditions. This study aims to identify ECM-driven molecular signatures to stratify the risk of RA and OA. METHODS: We integrated bulk transcriptomics data from 147 samples across five datasets, as well as scRNA-seq data from 88 samples comprising 349,921 cells. Differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and machine learning were employed to identify ECM-related hub genes. A risk score (RS) model based on ridge regression was established and validated. The RS was correlated with immune cell profiles, and a regulatory network involving miRNAs, mRNAs, transcription factors, and drugs was constructed. RESULTS: We identified eight ECM hub genes (SPARC, COL1A1, ANGPTL2, THY1, COL5A1, LRRC15, NID2, THBS3) that were significantly upregulated in RA and OA. The RS model stratified patients into high-risk and low-risk groups. The diagnostic performance of the model, as measured by AUC values, exceeded 0.8 across all cohorts. scRNA-seq and immune cell infiltration analyses revealed the involvement of these genes in ECM dysregulation. We predicted interaction between genes and multiple regulatory factors, in which the drug metoprolol was associated with LRRC15. CONCLUSIONS: We established an ECM-derived risk signature with robust diagnostic power, elucidating the shared mechanisms of ECM-immune dysregulation. Metoprolol was associated with LRRC15 in the disease cohort. This study provides a framework for precise diagnosis and targeted therapies.
abstract_zh: 背景：类风湿关节炎（rheumatoid arthritis, RA）和骨关节炎（osteoarthritis, OA）常并存，使诊断和治疗复杂化。细胞外基质（extracellular matrix, ECM）作为疾病进展的关键调节因子，在两种疾病中协调多层基质降解和炎症级联反应。本研究旨在识别ECM驱动的分子特征，以分层RA和OA的风险。方法：我们整合了来自五个数据集的147个样本的批量转录组学数据，以及来自88个样本的scRNA-seq数据，共包含349,921个细胞。采用差异表达分析、加权基因共表达网络分析和机器学习来识别ECM相关核心基因。基于岭回归建立风险评分（RS）模型并进行验证。将RS与免疫细胞谱相关联，并构建了涉及miRNA、mRNA、转录因子和药物的调控网络。结果：我们识别出八个ECM核心基因（SPARC、COL1A1、ANGPTL2、THY1、COL5A1、LRRC15、NID2、THBS3），这些基因在RA和OA中显著上调。RS模型将患者分为高风险组和低风险组。该模型的诊断性能，以AUC值衡量，在所有队列中均超过0.8。scRNA-seq和免疫细胞浸润分析揭示了这些基因在ECM失调中的参与。我们预测了基因与多种调控因子之间的相互作用，其中药物美托洛尔与LRRC15相关。结论：我们建立了一个具有稳健诊断能力的ECM衍生风险特征，阐明了ECM-免疫失调的共同机制。美托洛尔在疾病队列中与LRRC15相关。本研究为精准诊断和靶向治疗提供了框架。
